outcome: Any OTel backend renders sworn's runs as native LLM traffic: each dispatch exports a span carrying the GenAI semantic conventions - the real certified model id, the token split including cache and reasoning components, and wall-clock duration - with sworn's own facts riding as sworn.* attributes, and all spans of one run sharing one trace instead of randomized per-record identities.

exclude: export topology, channels, and where the emitter runs (S3's mechanism; this slice defines what a span says, exercised against a fixture sink through the existing serve-mediated path)
capture of the underlying facts (S1's mechanism; this slice projects what S1 journals)
backend-side concerns (verdict-to-score mapping is backend territory by ruling; the engine stays vendor-neutral)

waivers.reason: its tests reach internal/observe by import only; no cmd test pins span vocabulary, and the serve wiring is untouched by this slice

acceptance.text: A fixture OTLP sink receives one span per dispatch attempt carrying gen_ai.request.model (the certified model id actually dispatched), gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, the cache-read/cache-write/reasoning components when reported, and the attempt's duration - pinned by span-attribute goldens (anchor: internal/observe/telemetry_payload.go:197 - today exactly two synthetic span names, sworn.process.segment and sworn.recovery, and zero gen_ai.* attributes anywhere in the tree).

Spans of one run share one trace identity, so a backend renders the run as a single trace with dispatch spans inside it - replacing the per-record randomized trace and span ids at internal/observe/telemetry_payload.go:231 - and re-evaluation never exports duplicate span identities for the same attempt.

sworn's own facts ride as sworn.* attributes on the dispatch span: run, release, track, slice, role, responsibility, attempt/epoch/try, and transport status - pinned by the same goldens. No sworn.verdict attribute is emitted, and the goldens pin its absence: the r3 captain adjudication (operator-ratified in revision 4) established that no per-dispatch verdict exists on any read surface - effect state is completion state, sealed submissions are content-free by doctrine, and the slice-level last-known-wins outcome would state a false fact on a historical attempt span. The verdict attribute returns only when a content-free decision-outcome fact exists on a read surface (a later slice's write-seam, on the S9 pattern). No prompt, response, reasoning content, or session identifier appears in any attribute value.

Partial usage coverage is visible on the span itself: a span whose usage was not reported says so in-band (status attributes from S1's receipt vocabulary), never by silently omitting the attributes - pinned by a golden over a mixed-coverage fixture history.

constraints: Design ruling being encoded (2026-08-20): spans adopt OTel GenAI semantic conventions so any backend renders generations natively; sworn-specific facts ride as sworn.* attributes; verdict-to-score mapping is backend-side - the engine only emits attributes and stays vendor-neutral. Langfuse rendering the stream is operator-side evidence of the outcome, never a test dependency.

The existing sworn.eval metric projection and the cumulative segment span remain: this slice adds the per-dispatch span vocabulary; removals or renames of existing exported names are out of scope, and any payload schema growth is versioned honestly.
The 1024-attribute-group cardinality cap and the lossy non-blocking queue semantics of the telemetry runtime are unchanged (internal/observe/telemetry.go:17,113).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.

Revision 4 adjudications carried from the r3 captain receipt: the span name is sworn.dispatch; exactly the three pinned GenAI semconv keys are used verbatim (gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens) and cache/reasoning components ride as sworn.usage.* attributes - no unpinned keys are minted in the semconv namespace.

Revision 4 scope adjudication: the edit surface does NOT widen into internal/journal - the per-attempt effect identity is joinable inside internal/observe through the cockpit snapshot the evaluator already fetches (Snapshot.Runtime.Attempts carries EffectID; epoch/try parse from the effect id, slice from snapshot evidence, track from the graph), so S2 stays one mechanism in one package.
